slots.title: U.S. cash session — Sept. 8, 2026
slots.body:
U.S. equities closed lower on Sept. 8, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 1.2% at 52,786.07 and the S&P 500 off 0.6% at 7,674.13.
The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.3% to 26,423.69, and the Russell 2000 fell 0.5% to 2,960.20.

Oil was firm while stocks softened: Brent crude finished at 99.50 (+1.6%), and the United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in the tape) closed at 146.03 (+2.9%).
CNBC linked crude strength to U.S.–Iran tensions and supply concerns.
Barrons noted renewed Middle East strikes and a oil spike weighing on equities.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 8.2% to 15.72, from a prior close of 14.53.

At 10:00 ET the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index for August printed at 98.7, below the 99.3 estimate and down from 99.8 previously — a low-impact U.S. release in the economic calendar.

Among Nasdaq sector averages for the date, Financial Services lagged most at -1.7%, while Real Estate led at +1.7% and Industrials were up 1.1%.
Healthcare averaged -0.9%, Basic Materials -0.7%, and Technology -0.6%.

Megacap tech was mixed:
- $TSLA +4.0% to 368.16
- $ORCL +2.4% to 162.52
- $AMD +5.9% to 505.74
- $ASML +2.9%
- $TSM +2.4%
- $NVDA -2.0%

- $AAPL -1.2%

weighed on the growth complex.
